serpInvestigation.method: Claude-in-Chrome extension not connected, so the live Google SERP could not be driven. Used WebSearch on the top zero-click queries as a lower-fidelity substitute.
queries: how to find sleeper league id
how to find espn fantasy league id
serpInvestigation.finding: Both are answer-complete informational queries whose answer ('the number in your league URL') is one sentence, so a featured snippet / inline answer satisfies the searcher without a click - which is why a position-5 organic result takes ~0 clicks.
serpInvestigation.espn: ESPN publishes an official League-ID support page (support.espn.com). Google favours it and almost certainly shows a featured snippet from it. Our /league-id and /league-id/espn rank ~9-10, below the snippet and the official source. Low ROI to chase.
serpInvestigation.sleeper: No official Sleeper help article exists; top results are third-party dev/API docs. This is the one league-id family we can own. Our /league-id/sleeper already ranks top-5 with HowTo+FAQ schema; structuring the first on-page answer for snippet capture is the highest-leverage content fix in the cluster.
serpInvestigation.strategicConclusion: The /league-id cluster is high-impression, answer-complete, and low-intent for a draft tool; it will always convert poorly to clicks and worse to the product goal (creating a draw). The real growth lever is the TRANSACTIONAL cluster at positions 6-13: '[platform] draft order randomizer/generator' and 'how to randomize draft order on [platform]' (e.g. /sleeper at pos 6.15 for 'how to randomize draft order sleeper', 0 clicks). A click there is a likely product user. The guides.ts metaTitle comment already names this tension.
